summary:
What we developed was an interactive website that is displayed as an informative game, with the premise of the user conductive field missions, scans and in-depth analysis to complete tasks' objective. The missions are linked to a compelling story, which produces both educational content and emotional ties. 
The approach addresses the challenge by not only providing and highlighting detailed data about analogous sights and provide lists of locations we believe bear resemblance to Mars and Moons' climate, but also more detailed explanation as to why they bear such similarities in the first place.
We believe this is important because it encourages more people to interact with it since it's a game and add onto the feeling of immersion, and provide more than mere names to analogous sights that we hope to provide help to NASA and space agencies to carry out more successful missions.
details:
The project is displayed as an educational, interactive, role-playing game where the user immerses themselves as a scientist to complete objectives, playing a part of a bigger story. Upon entering the website, the user would be greeted with various fun and intriguing features that help them accompany us to discover analogous sights on Earth.


General websites which only contain data may bore people or confuse the users, so we converted this challenge into a game where the user may entertain themselves while learning about many helpful scientific facts and processes, which encourage usage more and generate more interest

We strive for the project to become an accessible, fun tool constantly updated for additional features and information for people in general, and the students and youth to become more interested in space and science, becoming more educated and informed, as well as spreading the spirit of learning.

We have used various software such as Claude, Gemini, Arena AI... to assist us with coding and to develop our project.

We believe that our project proves to be creative and stands out because we break free from the traditional way of presenting data and characterizing data. We use various sources to summarize data and present it in a way that catches people attention, and the right attention. We didn't choose to just simply show a graph or a map, but to actively visualize it and convey it in a way that catches people's attention, and help them better understand the materials.

We considered various factors such as accuracy, information, engagment, practicality, and more. We believe that our project, developed as a game, would be accessable and easy to update, our information is derived from trustworthy sources from NASA and reliable space agencies, as well as a boost in engagement in the format.
